record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: Classify Riemannian geodesic-orbit manifolds in the dimensions where no complete classification is known. A Riemannian homogeneous manifold M=G/K with metric g is a geodesic-orbit, or g.o., manifold when every geodesic is homogeneous with respect to the largest connected isometry group, meaning that each geodesic through the origin o can be written as gamma(t)=exp(tX).o for some nonzero X in the Lie algebra of G. What is a complete classification of such g.o. manifolds, especially in dimension 7 and in dimensions greater than 7?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Riemannian homogeneous manifold $M=G/K$ with $G$-invariant metric $g$, where $G$ is the largest connected group of isometries of $(M,g)$, is called a geodesic-orbit (g.o.) manifold if every geodesic of $(M,g)$ is the orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of $G$. Equivalently, for every geodesic $\gamma(t)$ starting at the origin $o=eK$, there exists a nonzero element $X$ in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$ such that $\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\cdot o$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.

Complete classifications of Riemannian g.o. manifolds are known only in low dimensions (e.g., up to dimension 6). 

Problem: Provide a complete classification of Riemannian g.o. manifolds $M=G/K$ in dimension $7$, and more generally in every dimension $n>7$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2020–2025) continues to produce new examples and partial classifications of g.o. manifolds—including 7-dimensional constructions, naturally reductive 7- and 8-dimensional spaces (Storm, 2020), and g.o. nilmanifolds (Nikonorov and others, 2024)—but no complete classification of Riemannian geodesic-orbit manifolds in dimension 7 or in higher dimensions is available. The general classification problem remains open.
